purpose: Moves CSS minification from print-time to enqueue-time and registers core 'path' data so WP 6.3+ wp_maybe_inline_styles() can inline the plugin's minified and combined CSS, while guarding the combine/minify pipelines against double-inlining core-inlineable styles.
riskRationale: The design is backward-compatible (all new core calls gated by function_exists) and the hook ordering was verified correct, but the inline-budget prediction helpers hardcode a 40KB default (core uses 20KB before WP 6.9) and apply a per-file check where core enforces a cumulative, smallest-first budget — silently dropping the combine/preload benefits on WP 6.3-6.8 and on style-heavy pages. The commit also adds ~4,700 dev-only files to the tracked vendor/ tree against the documented production-only vendor convention.
breakingChanges: On WP 6.3+, styles carrying path data registered by core or third parties (when over core's inline budget) are no longer minified by the minify_css() filter
The combined-CSS <link rel="preload"> is suppressed whenever the combined file is predicted to fit core's inline budget

text: A well-researched PR that correctly diagnoses the root timing problem — minify_css() ran on style_loader_tag, after core's inline pass — and fixes it by moving minification to enqueue time with path-data registration, preserving the legacy path on WP < 6.3 via function_exists() guards. The main weaknesses are that the inline-size-limit helpers diverge from core's actual algorithm (hardcoded 40KB default vs 20KB on WP < 6.9; per-file vs cumulative budget), the cache-reuse combine branch is inconsistent with the fresh branch, and the commit ships the entire dev vendor tree (~4,700 files) into tracked vendor/.

reasoning: The core mechanism is sound, well-guarded and tested, but three important issues remain before merge: the version-unaware 40KB inline budget and the per-file inline prediction both mispredict core's decision on WP 6.3-6.8 and style-heavy pages (silently regressing combine/preload behavior), the cache-reuse combine branch can double-inline styles, and the tracked vendor/ tree is bloated with dev-only packages. All have small, safe fixes.

message: Correct architectural pivot: rewriting styles at enqueue time (wp_enqueue_scripts priority PHP_INT_MAX-1) runs before core's wp_head priority-1 inline pass (verified on WP 6.3 and 6.9), so path data registered here is honored by wp_maybe_inline_styles() — the timing fix the issue actually required.
Every new core API call is gated behind function_exists('wp_maybe_inline_styles'), so WP < 6.3 keeps the fully intact legacy style_loader_tag rewriting path with no behavior change.

The style_loader_tag path-data guard is the correct mechanism to prevent double re-emission and re-minification of handles already rewritten at enqueue time (which would otherwise emit duplicate <link> tags and re-minify under a new md5 name every request).

register_combine_css_path() guards on both function_exists() and is_file() before calling wp_style_add_data(), so a missing combined file (e.g. non-direct filesystem or cleared cache) can never leave stale path data or trigger core's _doing_it_wrong.

core_will_inline() correctly implements the issue's Option A: core-inlineable path-data styles are left enqueued at their own queue position instead of being duplicated into the combined file, and suppressing the <link rel="preload"> echo when the combined file will be inlined avoids a wasted request.

The 12 Brain Monkey/PHPUnit tests meaningfully cover the negative gates (function_exists, combineCSS bail, non-all media skip, missing-file skip, path-data early return, size-budget detection) with clean temp-file lifecycle management and reflection helpers; all 12 pass and the changed PHP files are PHPCS-clean.

get_styles_inline_limit() hardcodes 40000 as the styles_inline_size_limit default, but core's default is 20000 on WP 6.3-6.8 (raised to 40KB only in 6.9, 50KB in 7.0). On WP 6.3-6.8, core_will_inline() and will_combine_css_inline() therefore over-predict inlining for the 20-40KB band: such path-data styles are skipped from the combined file yet core prints them as separate requests, and the combined file's <link rel="preload"> is suppressed for a file core serves as a normal stylesheet.
suggestion: Make the fallback version-aware so the plugin's prediction matches core's actual default on the running WP version, still passing it through the styles_inline_size_limit filter so site-level overrides win.

message: core_will_inline() (and will_combine_css_inline()) predict core's decision with a per-file size check, but wp_maybe_inline_styles() applies a CUMULATIVE budget across all queued path-data styles, sorted ascending by size, breaking once the running total exceeds the limit. On style-heavy pages (block themes with many core block/global styles all carrying path data) a file that individually fits is often NOT inlined, so a style skipped from the combined file loads as a separate unminified request and the combined file's preload is suppressed even though core serves it externally.
suggestion: Replicate core's greedy smallest-first cumulative accounting: gather all queued path-data styles, sort by size ascending, and treat a handle as core-inlineable only if its size plus the running total of smaller styles stays within the limit; apply the same cumulative logic to the combined file in will_combine_css_inline(). If a faithful model is too complex, be conservative (e.g. only skip/suppress when clearly within budget).

message: This commit adds ~4,700 dev-only Composer packages (~526k insertions) to the tracked vendor/ tree (phpunit, brain/monkey, antecedent/patchwork, mockery, hamcrest, sebastian/*, nikic, phar-io, myclabs, staabm, theseer, squizlabs/wpcs, phpcsstandards, phpcompatibility, dealerdirect) and rewrites the committed autoloaders to load them, contradicting AGENTS.md's production-only vendor convention ('composer release' before 'git add vendor/'). The release pipeline currently self-heals via 'composer install --no-dev', but .distignore does not exclude the newly added dev dirs, so any packaging/deploy path that skips the composer step would ship PHPUnit and Patchwork (a monkey-patching library that installs a file:// stream wrapper) to end users.
suggestion: Run 'composer release' (composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader) before committing so only production packages land in vendor/, and add the new dev-only vendor directories to .distignore as belt-and-braces so test tooling can never ship in the plugin ZIP.

message: The cache-reuse branch registers path data on wppo-combine-css but does not apply the core_will_inline() skip guard, so an existing combined file (generated before this PR) that already embeds core-inlineable styles (e.g. block styles carrying path data) will be both inlined by core AND served inside the combined file — duplicate rules on the page — until the cache regenerates. The fresh branch was fixed but the reuse branch keeps the old behavior, leaving the two branches inconsistent about double-inlining.
suggestion: Align the reuse branch with the fresh branch: apply the same core_will_inline() skip when iterating styles in the freshness check so core-inlineable handles neither force regeneration nor are expected in the file, and invalidate/regenerate the combined file when the set of combined handles changes rather than reusing an old file that still embeds them.

message: The new minify_css() guard returns the tag unchanged for ANY handle carrying 'path' data, including path data registered by core or third-party themes/plugins rather than only handles rewritten by minify_queued_styles(). On WP 6.3+ such a handle whose file exceeds the inline budget (or one enqueued after the enqueue-time pass) now silently bypasses plugin minification, whereas master would have minified it. Impact is limited because most core path-data styles are already *.min.css, but it is a coverage regression for unminified third-party path-data styles.
suggestion: Scope the guard to handles the plugin actually processed — track them in an instance property when minify_queued_styles() sets path data and return early only for those, or prefix-check the path data against the plugin's own min cache directory so genuinely third-party path-data handles still fall through to legacy minification.

message: The new suite covers only the no-op/skip branches and the private helpers in isolation; the headline behavior — minify_queued_styles() actually rewriting a style's src/ver to the minified cache file and calling wp_style_add_data('path') — is never asserted. In addition, setUp() stubs apply_filters with returnArg(2), pinning the budget to the plugin's 40000 default, so the version-dependent default (20000 on WP 6.3-6.8) and the cumulative-budget divergence from core are invisible to CI.
suggestion: Add a happy-path test that mocks the minifier and asserts src/ver are rewritten and wp_style_add_data() is called with the minified path, a version-gated test asserting get_styles_inline_limit() returns 20000/40000 by WP version, and a multi-style cumulative-budget scenario for core_will_inline().

message: minify_queued_styles() re-implements the full per-style eligibility pipeline from minify_css() (exclude_css check, Util::get_local_path, wppo_exclude_minification filter, is_minified_asset_name, is_css_minified, 'all' media) as a second copy of the same decision logic. Two copies drift easily (they already differ subtly — minify_css() has no 'all' media check) and make future behavior changes risky.
suggestion: Extract the shared per-style eligibility decision into one private helper (e.g. should_minify_style($handle, $style_data)) used by both minify_queued_styles() and minify_css() so the enqueue-time and tag-time paths cannot diverge.

message: The new methods (minify_queued_styles, core_will_inline, register_combine_css_path, will_combine_css_inline, get_styles_inline_limit) are documented with '@since 3.9.0', but the plugin's declared version is 1.8.0, so the changelog tags are inconsistent with the versioning scheme used by the rest of the codebase.
suggestion: Use '@since 1.9.0' (or the next real release version) so the docblocks match the plugin's version numbering.

message: The PR frames this as a 'WP 6.3+' feature, but wp_maybe_inline_styles() and the styles_inline_size_limit filter have existed since WP 5.8 and the plugin supports WP 6.2+, so the function_exists() gate is always true on every supported version. The docblocks/comments claiming 'WP 6.3+' are inaccurate; only the default budget changed in 6.9. No functional impact, but the comments mislead future maintainers about which versions exercise the new path.
suggestion: Update the doc comments to say the path-data mechanism exists since WP 5.8 and note that only the inline-budget default changed in 6.9.
